EP40:E10 19200-23000 LORD HARRINGTON [Ambitious, Proud]: "And soon, we'll be connected to the Duchess of Ashburgh."
EP40:E11 23000-26200 CAMERA: Tight close-up profile of Lady Harrington, her eyes glistening with cruel satisfaction in the soft sunlight.
EP40:E12 23200-26000 LADY HARRINGTON [Malicious, Taunting]: "Imagine Juliana seeing this."

EP40:E28 53200-55800 ACTION: Rupert smooths the lapels of his coat, checking his posture as he waits for the bride.

output.summary: Coverage is incomplete: the source warning notes gaps that are unavailable, and the on-screen evidence runs only through EP40:E51 (scenes sc_001 to sc_004, ending at 110080 ms with a cut to black). Analysis rests solely on event text; the supplied metadata (logline and continuity notes) is not on-screen evidence and was not used for any claims. Lord and Lady Harrington arrive at the cathedral and discuss a Juliana they expect to be harmed, with the Duchess of Ashburgh connection implied. An elder nobleman and a Royal Guard confirm all entrances are covered, and the elder nobleman says Ashburgh will have a new Duke and Duchess by sunset and that its witch will be dead. Rupert and Catherine's wedding then proceeds, with a conspiratorial exchange at the altar. Whether Rupert and Catherine are knowing conspirators, the identities of the elder nobleman and guard beyond on-screen roles, and the fate of Juliana are not established by the visible evidence; these are reported as uncertain.

beats.description: Noble guests ascend the cathedral steps as the Harringtons arrive by carriage and are announced.

The Harringtons speak of connection to the Duchess of Ashburgh and of Juliana, whom Lord Harrington says will not be seeing anything for long; the exchange is ominous but its exact nature is not fully explained on screen.
The Harringtons take their pew and Lady Harrington hints at a sinister outcome 'after' the wedding.
On the balcony an elder nobleman confirms through a Royal Guard that all entrances are covered and voices a plan for Ashburgh's new rulers and the death of its witch by sunset.
Catherine enters the cathedral in a bridal gown to organ music and approaches the altar where Rupert waits.
Rupert and Catherine exchange flattering and smug remarks and a conspiratorial look at the altar before the scene cuts to black.

revelations.claim: The cathedral's exits are reportedly covered on the elder nobleman's orders, suggesting a planned containment of guests.

Why are all entrances being covered?

revelations.claim: Lord Harrington implies Juliana will soon be unable to see anything and mocks her unluckiness at this place, suggesting harm is planned against her.
